items.title: June unemployment rate remains at 3.0pct, Statistics Department
items.summary: The Statistics Department said the number of employed persons rose 0.01 per cent to 16.83 million in June 2026 (May 2026: 16.82 million persons), while the number of unemployed persons increased from 513,400 to 517,800, rising by 0.9 per cent month-on-month. "The labour force recorded a marginal month-on-month increase of 0.04 per cent to 17.34 million persons in June 2026 (May 2026: 17.34 million persons). It said the employees' category comprised 75.0 per cent of the total employed persons, increasing slightly by 0.02 per cent, reaching 12.61 million persons in June 2026 (May 2026: 12.61 million persons), while the number of own-account workers rose marginally by 0.04 per cent to register 3.15 million persons (May 2026: 3.15 million persons).

items.title: King orders comprehensive, transparent probe into TH RCI findings - Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has decreed that investigations into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) be conducted comprehensively and transparently, with no compromise. "I would like to take this opportunity to convey my highest appreciation for His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim's decree, which emphasised that investigations into the findings of the RCI on TH must be conducted comprehensively, transparently and without compromise, leaving no stone unturned," he said during a special sitting of Parliament today to debate the RCI report. Zulkifli said the decree was in line with the government's commitment to safeguarding the trust placed by TH depositors.

items.title: Zulkifli urges opposition MPs to return for Tabung Haji RCI debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has called for opposition members of Parliament to return to the Dewan Rakyat and debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji. He said the walkout was regrettable as the debate centred on an institution that held deep significance for Malaysia's Muslim community. Tabung Haji is one of them.

items.title: Malaysia-Hong Kong dual IPO listing framework to take effect next month
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The simplified dual initial public offering (IPO) listing framework between Malaysia and Hong Kong will take effect next month, further strengthening capital market linkages between the two economies. Loke said Bursa Malaysia had also been recognised as a Recognised Stock Exchange by Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Ltd (HKEX), enabling public limited companies listed on Bursa Malaysia to apply for a secondary listing in Hong Kong. He said the development would provide Malaysian companies with greater access to Hong Kong's capital market and investors.

items.title: King orders full probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has ordered a comprehensive and transparent investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). The Star reported that Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the King had instructed that the investigation be conducted without compromise, with no stone left unturned. Zulkifli said the Cabinet had unanimously reviewed the RCI report on July 29 and decided to make it public by tabling and debating it during the special parliamentary sitting.

items.title: Body of missing 7-year-old found 3km downstream
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: The body of a seven-year-old Indonesian boy who fell into a river near a supermarket in Persiaran Subang Indah yesterday has been found. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the boy's body was found at 10.59am today, about three kilometres from where he was believed to have fallen into the river. "The victim was found by personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station and the department's Water Rescue Team (PPDA).

items.title: Turkiye MPs back historic law on reintegrating Kurdish militants
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Turkish lawmakers on Monday voted through a bill offering limited amnesty for Kurdish PKK militants, a key step in the peace process that seeks to end decades of deadly violence. The law is Turkiye's first legislative step towards ending the conflict and comes 18 months after Abdullah Ocalan, the jailed founder of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), urged his followers to disarm. Ocalan has played a key role in efforts to end the conflict, issuing a historic call in February 2025 for his fighters to disarm and embrace democratic means to defend the rights of Turkiye's Kurdish minority.

items.title: SD Guthrie Q2 earnings nearly double to RM987mil on industrial development, downstream gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SD Guthrie Bhd's net profit nearly doubled to RM987 million in the second quarter ended June 30 from RM505 million a year earlier, driven by stronger contributions from its industrial development and downstream businesses. Revenue, however, fell 4.4 per cent to RM4.94 billion from RM5.17 billion, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. SD Guthrie said its industrial development segment recorded a pre-tax profit of RM529 million during the quarter, while its downstream business, SD Guthrie International, posted an eight per cent increase in pre-tax profit to RM136 million.

items.title: Several detained as police, MACC probe TH RCI findings - Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) have launched investigations into findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with several individuals detained over alleged misconduct. Zulkifli said the action demonstrated the government's commitment to ensuring that no party was protected if found to have abused power or breached the trust involving TH funds. Zulkifli said the investments were among matters being examined following the RCI's findings.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng says six proposals to help MSMEs rejected by govt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today said six measures he proposed to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) cope with rising costs and economic pressures had been rejected by the government. Lim said the measures were necessary to ensure the survival of 1.1 million MSMEs in Malaysia, which he said contributed 38 per cent to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP), accounted for 48 per cent of employment and nearly 13 per cent of total exports. The ministry also said the government had already implemented several measures to support MSMEs affected by rising operating costs, including RM5 billion in guarantees under the Business Financing Guarantee Company (SJPP).

items.title: Schools closed as Indonesia battles wildfires
items.summary: SURABAYA: Dozens of Indonesian schools were shuttered for a second day Tuesday against the spreading haze of wildfires plaguing the archipelago at the start of a long and intense dry season worsened by El Nino. In West Kalimantan on the island of Borneo that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, the mayor of Pontianak ordered schools closed due to the smoke wafting over the city from fires elsewhere. Indonesia is forecast to experience an unusually tough dry season this year with high risk for drought and wildfires due in part to the El Nino weather phenomenon, the BMKG weather agency has said.

items.title: Reforms help TH achieve record RM4.64bil investment income in 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) recorded its highest-ever investment income of RM4.64 billion last year following reforms to its investment strategy, governance and financial management, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the performance reflected the results of reforms implemented since 2018 to strengthen TH's financial position and improve the quality of its investments. "Tabung Haji has successfully recorded the highest investment income in its history, amounting to RM4.64 billion in 2025, as a result of improved investment quality as well as stronger governance and transparency in the management of the institution," he said.

items.title: 52,750 Rumah Selangorku units completed as of mid-2026
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A total of 52,750 Rumah Selangorku (RSKU) units involving 167 projects had been completed and handed over to buyers as of mid-2026, the Selangor State Legislative Assembly was told today. State Housing and Culture Committee chairman Datuk Borhan Aman Shah said another 34,287 RSKU units involving 68 projects were under construction during the same period. He said the achievement showed that the implementation of affordable housing provision in the state was on a positive trajectory towards achieving the target set by the state government.

items.title: Death toll in Gaza exceeds 75,000, says Palestinian ambassador
items.summary: MOSCOW: The death toll in the Gaza Strip has exceeded 75,000 since the escalation began in 2023, Palestinian Ambassador to Russia Abdel Hafiz Nofal said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. "According to available data, the total number of dead in the Gaza Strip has exceeded 75,000, and the number of injured has exceeded 250,000," the ambassador told Russian newspaper Izvestia . "Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu said, referring to the plan Hamas agreed to in late July.

items.title: Gamuda climbs ESG rankings
items.summary: KUALALUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has been recognised for its sustainability efforts after being included in TIME and Statista's World's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 list while also advancing to the highest four-star grading band under the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia index. Gamuda said its inclusion in the global list reflects the strength of its sustainability practices and disclosures, while reinforcing its position as a trusted partner in delivering infrastructure and development projects that support long-term economic and community outcomes. The company also recorded an improvement in its Bursa Malaysia FTSE4Good ESG rating to 3.7, lifting it into the highest four-star ESG grading band under the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index.

items.title: BNM issued five warning letters to Tabung Haji leadership over asset-liability gap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) had issued five warning letters to the Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and the Minister of Religious Affairs regarding the gap between TH’s assets and liabilities. “At the time, TH’s position posed a potential systemic risk to the country’s financial stability. Unfortunately, those letters were ignored by TH’s leadership,” he said.

items.title: Rehda hails 10-year housing roadmap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association Malaysia (Rehda) has welcomed the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, describing it as a comprehensive framework that will help shape the future of Malaysia's housing sector. Rehda said the policy's theme, "Humanising Housing", aligns with its long-held view that housing goes beyond the construction of physical structures and should focus on delivering quality, affordable, liveable and sustainable homes for Malaysians. Rehda Malaysia president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the association was particularly encouraged by the policy's emphasis on data-driven housing planning, including the use of big data analytics and housing projections based on locality, existing supply, vacancy rates, housing types, income levels and price categories.

items.title: Tabung Haji must never again be victim of political interests - Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) must never again become a victim of political interests, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said today. "TH is not owned by today's government, yesterday's government or any political party. TH is the trust of Malaysian Muslims," he said during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into TH.

items.title: 61 groups object to genetically modified rice field trial in Perak
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Sixty-one organisations have objected to a proposed confined field trial involving genetically modified MR219 rice in Kampung Kepayang, Perak. The coalition, comprising farmers, consumer, and environmental groups, said it submitted a formal objection to the Department of Biosafety's director-general via the Unified Public Consultation (UPC) website on Aug 7. It said the proposed trial raised concerns over potential genetic contamination of conventional and wild rice, while claiming Malaysia's Biosafety Act 2007 did not provide adequate statutory protection, legal liability or redress for farmers who might suffer economic losses from GM contamination.

items.title: Two men with combined 52 criminal records nabbed over Jasin KK Mart robbery
items.summary: JASIN, Aug 11 — Police have arrested two men believed to be involved in an armed robbery at a KK Mart convenience store in Taman Maju here on Aug 6. Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said the two suspects, aged 44 and 45, were arrested separately at about 4.30 pm yesterday. He said the first suspect was arrested by the roadside along Jalan PPJ 3 in Jasin town, while the second was arrested in Sagil, Tangkak, Johor.

items.title: High dividend pressure drove TH into risky investments, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pressure to maintain high annual dividend payouts drove Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to make high-risk investments that eventually resulted in losses amounting to billions of ringgit, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) identified 14 problematic investments linked to losses running into billions of ringgit, including Putrajaya Perdana, Al-Rawda, PT TH Indo Plantation, True Rich and FGV. He said the investments were approved between 2010 and 2017 following recommendations by TH's board.

items.title: DBKL cuts red tape for restaurants, food operators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) is moving to ease business operations for restaurant and food premises operators by introducing three major improvements aimed at streamlining services and cutting red tape across the federal capital. DBKL said the measures follow recent engagement sessions involving Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud, the Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Chinese Coffee Shop and Tea Shop Owners' Association, and the Malaysia Muslim Restaurant Operators Association (Presma). Under the new outdoor seating guidelines, operators can apply through DBKL branch offices based on their parliamentary constituency.

items.title: NEEAP 2.0 targets RM85.24b savings, 11.6 per cent reduction in energy demand by 2035
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The National Energy Efficiency Policy and Action Plan 2026–2035 (NEEAP 2.0) aims to deliver RM85.24 billion in utility savings, reduce national energy demand by 11.6 per cent, and achieve cumulative energy savings of 815,383 terajoules (TJ) by 2035. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who officiated the launch of the NEEAP 2.0 here today, said the plan is guided by the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act 2024. The plan is in line with key roadmaps in Malaysia, namely the National Energy Policy 2022–2040, National Energy Transition Roadmap, New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the 12th and 13th Malaysia Plan.

items.title: PwC review found TH in critical financial position, Dewan told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government in 2018 appointed one of the Big Four accounting firms to reassess Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) financial position and performance after concerns were raised over its accounts. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the new TH board appointed PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) to review the institution's financial position in accordance with applicable accounting standards. Zulkifli said the RCI also found that TH's financial reporting at the time did not accurately reflect its actual financial position.

items.title: Anwar says Perikatan neglecting Tabung Haji depositors after MPs walk out of RCI debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today slammed the opposition, accusing it of trying to divert attention from issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) by making him the subject of political polemics. “Do you want to debate about me or Tabung Haji? He also questioned the position taken by Perikatan Nasional (PN), which is anchored by PAS, particularly over the interests of TH depositors from various walks of life.

items.title: Police: 14-year-old girl arrested after allegedly injuring classmate with kerambit in Shah Alam
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 11 — Police today confirmed that a 14-year-old female student was arrested after allegedly injuring a classmate with a sharp object at a secondary school in Shah Alam. Shah Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the suspect had brought a kerambit and injured a male classmate with it at around 11.42am on August 5. “An arrest was subsequently made and the case is currently under investigation,” he said, confirming that a police report had been lodged.

items.title: Zulkifli: Tabung Haji now in much stronger position after institutional recovery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is now in a much stronger position after undergoing an institutional recovery process, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. “The government chose to give TH room to restore the institution first. “Alhamdulillah, the government wishes to express its highest appreciation to the new TH management and all parties involved who have restored TH to excellent health,” he said.

items.title: Tabung Haji launches booklet to explain RCI findings, to restore depositors’ confidence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 (Bernama) -- Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) today launched a major public enlightenment initiative on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH through the distribution of a special information booklet. The booklet, titled “Tabung Haji: Apa Sudah Jadi?” (Tabung Haji: What Happened?

items.title: Govt denies TH assets sold to non-Muslims, Chinese interests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has denied claims that assets belonging to Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) were sold to non-Muslims or Chinese interests as part of its restructuring exercise. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the assets transferred under the 2018 recovery plan were sold to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), a special-purpose vehicle wholly owned by the government. Zulkifli said TH had transferred underperforming and problematic assets worth RM9.7 billion to UJSB at a value of RM19.9 billion as part of a plan to close the institution's asset-liability gap, which stood at about RM10 billion at the time.

items.title: Govt’s over RM10b Tabung Haji bailout aimed at restoring finances, not taking over assets, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government rescued Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) through a bailout exceeding RM10 billion due to mismanagement and embezzlement, to restore its financial position and not to take over the institution’s assets, the Dewan Rakyat was informed today. He said this during the minister’s briefing session on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH and the efforts and actions taken to restore the financial position of the institution at the Special Sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today. The situation ultimately forced the Pakatan Harapan Government to bail out TH with a restructuring plan to restore its financial position so that TH could become solvent again and remain sustainable in the long term,” he added.

items.title: Typhoon Dolphin's vast storm system pushes inland, threatens central China
items.summary: XIANGYANG: Typhoon Dolphin churned deeper inland to the central Chinese province of Hubei on Tuesday, prompting the closure of tourist areas and suspension of construction projects, as forecasters warned of the danger of extreme rainfall in the province's mountainous northwest. Hubei authorities have issued a yellow warning for cities including Xiangyang, Huanggang and Suizhou, citing a heightened risk of flooding and landslides. Dolphin's peripheral airflow will be forced to rise when it encounters the mountains in Hubei's western region, causing rainfall to intensify several times over, Wang Xiaoling, deputy director of Hubei's provincial meteorological observatory, told local newspaper Hubei Daily.

items.title: RCI: TH crisis stems from years of weak governance, political interference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The financial crisis at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was the result of years of weak governance, political interference, risky investment decisions and failures to accurately reflect the institution's financial position, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. It was the accumulated result of greed and misconduct, weak governance, interference by certain interests, risky investment decisions and failure to transparently reflect its financial position," he said when explaining the government's position on the RCI report. He said reforms had also been introduced to strengthen TH's financial reporting and governance.

items.title: [UPDATED] Teen girl arrested for allegedly hurting classmate with kerambit at Shah Alam school
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 14-year-old female student was arrested after allegedly injuring a male classmate with a kerambit at a secondary school here on Aug 5. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the student suffered minor injuries to his arm. "The 14-year-old female student was arrested immediately following the incident and her statement was recorded to assist investigations.

items.title: [UPDATED] Zaliha slams PN MPs over walkout during Tabung Haji RCI debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman Datuk Dr Zaliha Mustafa has slammed Perikatan Nasional (PN) MPs for staging a walkout during a special Dewan Rakyat sitting to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) today. Zaliha, who is also PKR vice-president, said the walkout was disappointing, particularly as MPs had been given the opportunity to scrutinise, question and challenge the findings of the RCI report in Parliament. Zaliha said opposition MPs should not champion transparency, accountability and the interests of Muslims outside Parliament, only to leave the chamber when given the opportunity to debate the issues directly.

items.title: AI helps Asian airports squeeze more from existing capacity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) could help Asian airports handle rising passenger traffic by improving the use of existing runways, gates and terminals, reducing the need to wait years for costly infrastructure expansion, said Assaia chief executive officer Christiaan Hen. AI can identify bottlenecks during aircraft turnarounds in real time, allowing airport and airline teams to intervene before disruptions on the ground develop into flight delays, he said. AI offers a different approach by helping airports increase the capacity of existing infrastructure through efficient day-to-day operations and optimised resource allocation, he said.

items.title: Zulkifli: Five Bank Negara warnings over Tabung Haji's finances went unheeded
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) issued five warnings to Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2014 over the institution's widening asset-liability gap and the risks associated with paying high profit distributions, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the warnings came as TH's financial position deteriorated, with its reserves at risk of turning negative. He said BNM, although not TH's regulator, had raised concerns about the impact of high profit distributions on the institution's already low reserves.

items.title: Asean must protect vital sea lanes
items.summary: LETTER: IN an increasingly uncertain world, prudence — not power — is likely to be the region's greatest strategic asset besides robust domestic economic and security fundamentals. Asean has survived well by not getting entangled in big power politics. The region has several strategic straits used for international navigation that can be easily exploited by predatory powers.

items.title: Over 100 killed after strongest quake this century hits western Colombia
items.summary: BOGOTA: More than 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, toppling buildings, damaging hospitals and infrastructure and trapping people beneath the rubble in the country's strongest earthquake this century. "The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble." As night fell, rescue workers and volunteers with headlamps hurried to find people still trapped under rubble.

items.title: Malaysia aims to be Asia-Pacific's most connected nation - Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airports aims to make Malaysia the most connected country in the Asia-Pacific, supported by capacity expansion at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and a push for more direct international routes. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the strategy would also strengthen direct connectivity to Penang, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching, rather than focusing solely on Kuala Lumpur. "There are four direct flights between Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong just by Cathay Pacific.

items.title: Loke urges Hong Kong investors to explore Malaysia beyond Klang Valley
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong investors should look beyond Kuala Lumpur and the Klang Valley when exploring investment opportunities in Malaysia, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke. Loke said the government is adopting a multi-pronged strategy to spread economic growth nationwide, with regions offering distinct opportunities in semiconductors, renewable energy, and tourism. Present were Hong Kong Trade Development Council chairman Prof Frederick Ma and Hong Kong Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau.

items.title: Govt could have faced RM74.5b liability from Tabung Haji bank run in 2018, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government risked assuming liabilities of about RM74.5 billion if a massive panic withdrawal, or “bank run”, had occurred in 2018, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. He noted that a panic withdrawal did occur in 2019, involving net withdrawals of RM6 billion within a short period following the announcement of a 1.25 per cent hibah for 2018 in early 2019. How much panic withdrawal could have occurred?”

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: Malaysia’s renewable energy transition to catalyse RM4.3b investment, create 7,738 jobs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Malaysia’s renewable energy transition is expected to catalyse about RM4.3 billion in investments and create approximately 7,738 indirect employment opportunities through 42 projects approved under the 2026 Feed-in Tariff (FiT) e-bidding exercise, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. The successful projects comprise 16 biogas projects totalling 26.185MW, 11 biomass projects totalling 135.94MW and 15 small hydropower projects totalling 169.23MW. Akmal said the FiT mechanism would also help Malaysia diversify its renewable energy sources by incorporating biomass, biogas and small hydropower into the country’s energy mix.

items.title: Opposition walks out after Speaker rejects deferment of special Tabung Haji RCI sitting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Opposition lawmakers walked out almost immediately after today’s special parliamentary sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji convened. Earlier, Kota Bharu MP Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the sitting should be deferred until the prime minister recovers and resumes his duties. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is currently undergoing physiotherapy treatment after undergoing an elective laparoscopic surgery procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker confirms Wong Chen’s resignation as Subang MP, says EC notified of vacancy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul today confirmed Wong Chen’s resignation as Subang MP. He said that he has informed the Election Commissions (EC) regarding the matter. “I have informed the EC of the vacancy in the Subang parliamentary seat in accordance with Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution” he said before the start of the special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Man arrested after trying to open Batik Air emergency door at 9,144m on flight from Malaysia to India
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A man was arrested after allegedly attempting to open an emergency exit door while travelling on a Batik Air flight from Malaysia to India at an altitude of about 9,144 metres. According to People, the 36-year-old suspect, identified as Jamsheer Athanikkal, allegedly behaved erratically during the flight, which had departed from Malaysia for India recently. Video footage of the incident shared on social media showed several crew members restraining Jamsheer with zip ties.

items.title: Man dies after car carrying rice sacks crashes into ditch in Tanah Merah
items.summary: Kemahang Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Mat Nuri Muhamad said the department received an emergency call via NG999 at 11.44pm, according to Sinar Harian . He said firefighters arrived at the scene at 11.50pm and found the Proton Wira overturned in the ditch. He said the operation, which involved five firefighters, ended at 12.28am.

items.title: Anwar thanks well-wishers, to follow special Parliament sitting on Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has thanked everyone who prayed for his wellbeing and sent him birthday wishes as he turns 79 today. Anwar also apologised for being unable to attend the special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji from 2014 to 2020. Anwar also prayed for the smooth conduct of the special sitting.

items.title: Rafizi: Govt has yet to fully settle RM12.5b Tabung Haji commitment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government has yet to fully settle its RM12.5 billion financial commitment to Lembaga Tabung Haji following the maturity of a Sukuk Urusan Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) instrument in May, former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said. “The Sukuk UJSB Series 1 matured on May 29, 2026. Rafizi said the financial restructuring of Tabung Haji approved by the government in late 2018 involved the federal government, through wholly owned company Urusan Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), taking over loss-making Tabung Haji assets at values higher than their actual worth.

items.title: Seven-year-old boy feared drowned after falling into river in Subang Jaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A seven-year-old Indonesian boy is feared drowned after falling into a river at Persiaran Subang Indah, near a supermarket in Subang Jaya, last night. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Assistant Director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 8.06 pm. He said a team from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene and arrived 10 minutes later.

items.title: Three Malaysians detained in Taiwan over alleged scam mule activities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Three Malaysians were detained in Kaohsiung, Taiwan last month for allegedly acting as money mules for a scam syndicate. Central News Agency (CNA) reported yesterday that the three male suspects, aged 18, 26 and 39, entered Taiwan as tourists before being detained separately, according to Berita Harian . The 39-year-old suspect was reportedly detained in front of a post office ATM, with police seizing NT$155,000 (RM19,050) in cash, two bank cards and a mobile phone.

items.title: Mindef channels RM275.4m to MAF veterans’ welfare programmes this year
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 11 — The Ministry of Defence (Mindef) has channeled RM275.4 million, or 90 per cent, of the RM303.3 million allocated to the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) to the Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV) this year. The ministry has also approved 34 new home construction projects and 323 home repair projects for MAF veterans to date. Mindef also confirmed that education support for veterans’ children will continue.

items.title: Sri Aman forest fire spreads to 100ha, feared to worsen Sarawak haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A forest fire in Sri Aman has spread across about 100 hectares, raising concerns that it could worsen haze conditions in Sarawak as air quality deteriorates due to transboundary smoke. A spokesperson for the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said the fire, which started around noon yesterday, had spread across about 100 hectares of forest along Jalan Kejatau-Lingga, Sri Aman, according to a Harian Metro report. He said the department received a call about the incident at 1.19pm before a team from the Sri Aman Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene to conduct firefighting operations.

items.title: Ahmad Zahid visits Ismail Sabri at IJN, prays for former PM’s recovery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday visited former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is currently receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here. In a post on X, Ahmad Zahid also prayed for the Bera Member of Parliament’s recovery and continued good health. Ahmad Zahid also prayed that Ismail Sabri would be able to resume his service and daily activities as usual.

items.title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as 11 areas record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Haze conditions in Sarawak have worsened, with the number of areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising to 11 as of 6am today. Besides Serian, 10 other monitoring stations also recorded API readings in the unhealthy category. API readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy.

items.title: AirBorneo joins FLYsiswa, offers RM400 flight subsidy to eligible students
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 11 — AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd has joined the government-backed FLYsiswa air travel subsidy initiative, offering eligible Malaysian students a RM400 digital voucher to subsidise domestic economy flight tickets, the airline said in a statement today. According to AirBorneo, the initiative, spearheaded by the Transport Ministry, is aimed at easing travel costs for students studying away from their home states, particularly those travelling between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan. AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said the cost of air travel should not become an obstacle for students who need to return home during semester breaks, festive periods or emergencies.

items.title: Malaysian detained in India after 4kg of hydroponic cannabis found in luggage
items.summary: CHENNAI, Aug 11 — A Malaysian national was detained by Indian authorities after allegedly carrying 4.033 kilogrammes of high-grade hydroponic cannabis through Chennai International Airport, India. The arrest was made by officers from the Chennai Customs Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) after the suspect arrived from Bangkok on Friday night, based on passenger profiling, Sinar Harian reported. An X-ray scan of the suspect’s checked luggage detected suspicious images, prompting a detailed inspection.

items.title: Malaysia ready to strengthen defence ties with Iran, says Mohamed Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Malaysia is ready to expand and strengthen more substantive defence cooperation with Iran based on the close friendship between the two countries. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said this was conveyed during his telephone conversation with Iran’s Acting Minister of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics, Brigadier General Seyed Majid Ebn-e-Reza. In a Facebook post yesterday, he said Malaysia also hoped that a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on defence cooperation could be finalised as an official instrument to strengthen defence ties between the two countries.

items.title: Anwar sues PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim over alleged defamatory remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today filed a defamation suit against PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man over remarks made during a ceramah (political speech) in Pahang last June. Anwar, as the plaintiff, filed the suit through the law firm S.N. Nair & Partners at the High Court here, naming Tuan Ibrahim as the defendant.

items.title: Simplified: The Tabung Haji RCI report and what it said
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Today, in a special sitting of Parliament, MPs are expected to debate a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the country’s Muslim pilgrims’ fund Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Currently, TH manages the savings of over 9.8 million depositors. What is the RCI about?

items.title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns bright among older Malaysians
items.summary: That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year’s National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating Merdeka (Independence) remain fresh in their minds. The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories. With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.
